summary: Discover the intricacies of petroleum operations with our Cost Audit and Accounting Course. Equip yourself with the tools to manage costs effectively.
lede: Petroleum accounting covers how finance and audit professionals in upstream oil and gas track, verify, and report costs across joint ventures. Participants learn to interpret contract accounting procedures, compare project spending with approved budgets, reconcile joint interest billings, and assess cost-recovery calculations, with practice in audit planning and procurement reviews.
audienceIntro: This course is essential for finance and audit professionals who operate within the high-stakes environment of upstream oil and gas exploration and production.
audience: Finance Managers in National Oil Companies (NOCs)
modules: Upstream Fiscal Regimes and Contractual Frameworks
Petroleum Accounting Standards and IFRS® 6 Compliance
Joint Operating Agreements and Accounting Procedures
Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) and Capital Budgeting
Joint Interest Billing (JIB) and Revenue Accounting
Cost Recovery Mechanisms and Profit Oil Calculations
Petroleum Audit Planning and Risk Assessment
Field Operations and Procurement Audit Techniques
Digital Transformation and AI in Petroleum Auditing
prerequisites: Participants should have a minimum of 3-5 years of experience in finance, accounting, or internal audit, preferably within the energy or extractive industries. Familiarity with basic Joint Operating Agreement (JOA) concepts and general IFRS® principles is highly recommended. No prior advanced petroleum auditing knowledge is required, though experience with any ERP system is beneficial.
